newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian Indians hijack bus, take hostages.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian Indians hijack bus, take hostages.

text.p: Indians have hijacked a bus in northern Brazil and may be demanding a teacher for their village children as ransom, a newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said Guajajara Indians blocked a road with logs near the town of Grajau in Maranhao state and took the driver and an undetermined number of passengers hostage.

The paper said the motive for the abductions was not clear but that last month, Indians of the same tribe kidnapped three officials from the Maranhao state education ministry, demanding a teacher be sent to work in their village.
"We still don't have any concrete information," Jackson George, an official of the National Indian Foundation's (Funai) branch office in the state capital Sao Luis, told Folha.
Neither local police nor Funai officials could immediately be reached for comment.
The 10,200 Guajajara Indians in Maranhao have a reputation for not shirking conflict.

In July last year, they clashed with landless families settling on their territory and in 1992 fought the construction of a road and blocked a railway used by state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, demanding compensation.
